# About this task

## Task objective

Build a reusable Quarto report that can be rendered for different study settings by changing parameter values instead of manually rewriting the report.

# Report parameters

The values below are supplied through the YAML `params` section at the top of this file.

| Parameter | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `study_id` | Study identifier shown in the report |
| `study_title` | Report title for the study |
| `treatment_group` | `All`, `Placebo`, `Drug A` or `Drug B` |
| `number_of_subjects` | Number of synthetic subjects to generate |
| `number_of_lab_records` | Number of synthetic laboratory records to generate |
| `random_seed` | Seed used to make data generation reproducible |

You can change these values in the YAML header and render the report again. The same report structure will be reused with the new inputs.

# Prepare the R environment

This report uses the following packages:

- `data.table` for data manipulation, filtering, joins and summaries.
- `ggplot2` for plots.
- `knitr` for formatted tables.

The setup chunk checks whether the packages are installed. It installs missing packages from CRAN if needed.

```{r setup}
required_packages <- c("data.table", "ggplot2", "knitr")

installed_packages <- rownames(installed.packages())
missing_packages <- setdiff(required_packages, installed_packages)

if (length(missing_packages) > 0) {
  install.packages(
    missing_packages,
    repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org"
  )
}

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(data.table)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(knitr)
})

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  fig.width = 8,
  fig.height = 5,
  dpi = 120
)
```

# Create the project folders

The report creates the required folders automatically. They will be created relative to the current working directory used to render this Quarto file.

```{r create-folders}
project_folders <- c(
  "data",
  "results",
  "results/tables",
  "results/figures",
  "reports",
  "documentation",
  "logs"
)

for (folder in project_folders) {
  dir.create(
    folder,
    recursive = TRUE,
    showWarnings = FALSE
  )
}

cat("Project folders are ready.\n")
cat("Working directory:", getwd(), "\n")
```

Expected folder structure:

```text
Task_26_Quarto_Reporting/
|
|-- data/
|-- results/
|   |-- tables/
|   |-- figures/
|-- reports/
|-- documentation/
|-- logs/
|
|-- Task_26_Quarto_Reporting.qmd
```

# Display the report information

The following values come from the YAML parameters. This is what makes the report reusable.

```{r report-information}
study_id <- params$study_id
study_title <- params$study_title
selected_treatment <- params$treatment_group

cat("Study ID:", study_id, "\n")
cat("Study title:", study_title, "\n")
cat("Treatment selection:", selected_treatment, "\n")
cat("Report date:", as.character(Sys.Date()), "\n")
```

**Study ID:** `r params$study_id`

**Study title:** `r params$study_title`

**Treatment selection:** `r params$treatment_group`

**Report generated on:** `r Sys.Date()`

# Generate synthetic clinical-style datasets

For this exercise, we create two simplified datasets:

- ADSL: one record per subject.
- ADLB: multiple laboratory records per subject.

The number of rows is controlled by the YAML parameters.

```{r generate-data}
set.seed(params$random_seed)

n_subjects <- as.integer(params$number_of_subjects)
n_lab_records <- as.integer(params$number_of_lab_records)

if (
  length(n_subjects) != 1 ||
  is.na(n_subjects) ||
  n_subjects < 1
) {
  stop("number_of_subjects must be a positive whole number.")
}

if (
  length(n_lab_records) != 1 ||
  is.na(n_lab_records) ||
  n_lab_records < 1
) {
  stop("number_of_lab_records must be a positive whole number.")
}

# ADSL: one row per subject.
adsl <- data.frame(
  USUBJID = sprintf("SUBJ%05d", seq_len(n_subjects)),
  AGE = sample(18:80, n_subjects, replace = TRUE),
  SEX = sample(c("F", "M"), n_subjects, replace = TRUE),
  TRT01A = sample(
    c("Placebo", "Drug A", "Drug B"),
    n_subjects,
    replace = TRUE
  ),
  COUNTRY = sample(
    c("India", "USA", "UK", "Germany"),
    n_subjects,
    replace = TRUE
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# ADLB: laboratory records linked to subjects in ADSL.
adlb <- data.frame(
  USUBJID = sample(
    adsl$USUBJID,
    n_lab_records,
    replace = TRUE
  ),
  PARAMCD = sample(
    c("ALT", "AST", "HB", "WBC", "CREAT"),
    n_lab_records,
    replace = TRUE
  ),
  AVAL = round(
    rnorm(n_lab_records, mean = 50, sd = 12),
    2
  ),
  VISIT = sample(
    c("Baseline", "Week 4", "Week 8", "Week 12"),
    n_lab_records,
    replace = TRUE
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Convert both datasets to data.table objects.
# setDT() converts by reference, avoiding an unnecessary full copy.
data.table::setDT(adsl)
data.table::setDT(adlb)

# Save the generated datasets for review and reuse.
write.csv(
  adsl,
  "data/synthetic_adsl.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  adlb,
  "data/synthetic_adlb.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

cat("ADSL records:", nrow(adsl), "\n")
cat("ADLB records:", nrow(adlb), "\n")
```

# Basic data checks

Before creating summaries, perform a few simple checks.

```{r data-checks}
adsl_has_unique_subjects <- !anyDuplicated(adsl$USUBJID)

adlb_subjects_exist <- all(
  adlb$USUBJID %in% adsl$USUBJID
)

data_check_results <- data.frame(
  CHECK = c(
    "ADSL subject identifiers are unique",
    "All ADLB subject identifiers exist in ADSL"
  ),
  STATUS = ifelse(
    c(adsl_has_unique_subjects, adlb_subjects_exist),
    "PASS",
    "FAIL"
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

knitr::kable(
  data_check_results,
  caption = "Basic input data checks"
)

write.csv(
  data_check_results,
  "results/tables/data_check_results.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

if (!all(data_check_results$STATUS == "PASS")) {
  stop("One or more basic data checks failed.")
}
```

# Apply the treatment parameter

The report can display all treatment groups or one selected group.

Valid values are:

- `All`
- `Placebo`
- `Drug A`
- `Drug B`

```{r filter-treatment}
valid_treatments <- c("All", "Placebo", "Drug A", "Drug B")

if (!selected_treatment %in% valid_treatments) {
  stop(
    "Invalid treatment_group. Use All, Placebo, Drug A or Drug B."
  )
}

if (selected_treatment == "All") {
  adsl_analysis <- adsl
} else {
  # data.table row filtering: DT[i, ]
  adsl_analysis <- adsl[TRT01A == selected_treatment]
}

# Add treatment information to each laboratory record.
# This data.table join keeps the laboratory records and brings in TRT01A.
adlb_with_treatment <- adlb[
  adsl[, .(USUBJID, TRT01A)],
  on = "USUBJID",
  nomatch = 0
]

if (selected_treatment == "All") {
  adlb_analysis <- adlb_with_treatment
} else {
  adlb_analysis <- adlb_with_treatment[
    TRT01A == selected_treatment
  ]
}

cat("Subjects included:", nrow(adsl_analysis), "\n")
cat("Laboratory records included:", nrow(adlb_analysis), "\n")
```

# Study overview

This section provides a high-level summary of the selected study population.

```{r study-overview}
study_overview <- data.frame(
  STUDY_ID = study_id,
  STUDY_TITLE = study_title,
  TREATMENT_SELECTION = selected_treatment,
  TOTAL_SUBJECTS_GENERATED = nrow(adsl),
  SUBJECTS_INCLUDED = nrow(adsl_analysis),
  TOTAL_LAB_RECORDS_GENERATED = nrow(adlb),
  LAB_RECORDS_INCLUDED = nrow(adlb_analysis),
  REPORT_DATE = as.character(Sys.Date()),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

knitr::kable(
  study_overview,
  caption = "Study overview"
)

write.csv(
  study_overview,
  "results/tables/study_overview.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

# Demographic summary

We summarize the number of subjects and age information by treatment group.

```{r demographic-summary}
demographic_summary <- adsl_analysis[
  ,
  .(
    N_SUBJECTS = .N,
    MEAN_AGE = round(mean(AGE), 1),
    SD_AGE = round(sd(AGE), 1),
    MIN_AGE = min(AGE),
    MAX_AGE = max(AGE)
  ),
  by = TRT01A
][order(TRT01A)]

knitr::kable(
  demographic_summary,
  caption = "Demographic summary by treatment group"
)

write.csv(
  demographic_summary,
  "results/tables/demographic_summary.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

## Subject counts by sex

```{r sex-summary}
sex_summary <- adsl_analysis[
  ,
  .(N_SUBJECTS = .N),
  by = .(TRT01A, SEX)
][order(TRT01A, SEX)]

knitr::kable(
  sex_summary,
  caption = "Subject counts by treatment and sex"
)

write.csv(
  sex_summary,
  "results/tables/sex_summary.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

# Demographic visualization

The following histogram displays the age distribution of the selected subjects.

```{r}
#| label: age-histogram
#| fig-cap: "Age distribution of selected subjects"

age_plot <- ggplot(
  adsl_analysis,
  aes(x = AGE)
) +
  geom_histogram(
    binwidth = 5,
    boundary = 0,
    color = "white"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Age Distribution",
    subtitle = paste("Study:", study_id),
    x = "Age in years",
    y = "Number of subjects"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

age_plot
```

Save the plot as a PNG file.

```{r save-age-plot}
ggsave(
  filename = "results/figures/age_distribution.png",
  plot = age_plot,
  width = 8,
  height = 5,
  dpi = 300
)
```

# Laboratory analysis

We summarize laboratory values by treatment group and parameter.

The values in this example are simulated. They are not clinical reference ranges and must not be used for medical interpretation.

```{r laboratory-summary}
laboratory_summary <- adlb_analysis[
  ,
  .(
    N_RECORDS = sum(!is.na(AVAL)),
    MEAN_AVAL = round(mean(AVAL, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    SD_AVAL = round(sd(AVAL, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    MIN_AVAL = round(min(AVAL, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    MAX_AVAL = round(max(AVAL, na.rm = TRUE), 2)
  ),
  by = .(TRT01A, PARAMCD)
][order(TRT01A, PARAMCD)]

knitr::kable(
  laboratory_summary,
  caption = "Laboratory summary by treatment and parameter"
)

write.csv(
  laboratory_summary,
  "results/tables/laboratory_summary.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

# Laboratory visualization

The boxplot displays the distribution of laboratory values by treatment group. Each panel represents one laboratory parameter.

```{r}
#| label: laboratory-boxplot
#| fig-cap: "Laboratory value distributions by treatment group"

laboratory_plot <- ggplot(
  adlb_analysis,
  aes(
    x = TRT01A,
    y = AVAL
  )
) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ PARAMCD,
    scales = "free_y"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Laboratory Values by Treatment",
    subtitle = paste("Study:", study_id),
    x = "Treatment group",
    y = "Laboratory value"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 30,
      hjust = 1
    )
  )

laboratory_plot
```

Save the plot as a PNG file.

```{r save-laboratory-plot}
ggsave(
  filename = "results/figures/laboratory_boxplot.png",
  plot = laboratory_plot,
  width = 10,
  height = 7,
  dpi = 300
)
```

# R and package session information

Session information helps another programmer understand the environment in which the report was generated.

It records the R version, operating system and package versions.

```{r session-information}
cat("R version:\n")
print(R.version.string)

cat("\nPlatform:\n")
print(R.version$platform)

package_versions <- data.frame(
  PACKAGE = c("data.table", "ggplot2", "knitr"),
  VERSION = vapply(
    c("data.table", "ggplot2", "knitr"),
    function(package_name) {
      as.character(packageVersion(package_name))
    },
    character(1)
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

knitr::kable(
  package_versions,
  caption = "Package versions used in this report"
)

write.csv(
  package_versions,
  "results/tables/package_versions.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

sessionInfo()

# Output inventory

The following code lists the files created during report execution.

```{r output-inventory}
output_directories <- c(
  "data",
  "results",
  "documentation"
)

output_inventory <- unlist(
  lapply(
    output_directories,
    function(folder) {
      if (dir.exists(folder)) {
        list.files(
          folder,
          recursive = TRUE,
          full.names = FALSE
        )
      } else {
        character(0)
      }
    }
  )
)

inventory_table <- data.frame(
  FILE = output_inventory,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

knitr::kable(
  inventory_table,
  caption = "Files generated by this Quarto report"
)

writeLines(
  output_inventory,
  "results/output_inventory.txt"
)
```

# Final checks

The report should complete with the following conditions:

- Synthetic ADSL and ADLB datasets were generated.
- Basic dataset checks passed.
- The requested treatment selection was applied.
- Demographic and laboratory summary tables were generated.
- Age and laboratory plots were generated.
- CSV and PNG output files were saved.
- R and package session information was recorded.

```{r final-checks}
final_checks <- data.frame(
  CHECK = c(
    "ADSL dataset created",
    "ADLB dataset created",
    "Study overview created",
    "Demographic summary created",
    "Laboratory summary created",
    "Age plot saved",
    "Laboratory plot saved",
    "Report summary saved"
  ),
  STATUS = c(
    file.exists("data/synthetic_adsl.csv"),
    file.exists("data/synthetic_adlb.csv"),
    file.exists("results/tables/study_overview.csv"),
    file.exists("results/tables/demographic_summary.csv"),
    file.exists("results/tables/laboratory_summary.csv"),
    file.exists("results/figures/age_distribution.png"),
    file.exists("results/figures/laboratory_boxplot.png"),
    file.exists("documentation/task26_report_summary.txt")
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

final_checks$RESULT <- ifelse(
  final_checks$STATUS,
  "PASS",
  "FAIL"
)

knitr::kable(
  final_checks,
  caption = "Final report generation checks"
)

if (!all(final_checks$STATUS)) {
  stop("One or more report output checks failed.")
}

cat("\nAll final checks passed.\n")
```

# How to render this report

## Option 1: Render from RStudio

1. Open `Task_26_Quarto_Reporting.qmd` in RStudio.
2. Confirm that the working directory is the project folder.
3. Click **Render**.
4. Quarto will execute the code and generate the HTML report in the `reports` folder.

## Option 2: Render from the R console

```{r render-command, eval=FALSE}
quarto::quarto_render(
  "Task_26_Quarto_Reporting.qmd"
)
```

You can also render from the terminal:

```bash
quarto render Task_26_Quarto_Reporting.qmd
```

## Render with different parameters

The template can be reused for another treatment group without editing the report's analysis code.

For example, run the following from the R console after saving the QMD file:

```r
quarto::quarto_render(
  "Task_26_Quarto_Reporting.qmd",
  execute_params = list(
    study_id = "STUDY-002",
    study_title = "Second Synthetic Clinical Study",
    treatment_group = "Drug A",
    number_of_subjects = 1500,
    number_of_lab_records = 7500,
    random_seed = 2027
  )
)
```

Try changing `treatment_group` to `"Placebo"`, `"Drug B"` or `"All"`.

Task 26 can be considered complete when:

- [ ] The Quarto file contains a consistent YAML header.
- [ ] Study inputs are controlled through parameters.
- [ ] Synthetic datasets are generated and saved.
- [ ] Demographic and laboratory tables are created.
- [ ] Plots are created and saved.
- [ ] Session information and package versions are recorded.
- [ ] The report renders successfully from a clean R session.
- [ ] The report can be reused with different parameter values.
- [ ] The generated output files are reviewed.
